Classic Italian Rainbow Cookie

Fancy a snack that’s as colorful as a toddler’s crayon box? These Classic Italian Rainbow Cookies are the kind of treat that’ll make you feel like a kid again—only with better flavor and no messy fingers (mostly).

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 30 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

For the cookies

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of milk
  • a pinch of salt
  • a stick of cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
  • a couple of egg yolks

For the filling

  • a heaping tablespoon of almond butter
  • a few tablespoons of powdered sugar
  • a dash of vanilla extract

For the rainbow coating

  • a bag of colorful non-pareil sprinkles
  • a few drops of food coloring (optional)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, and butter. Use your hands or a pastry cutter to work the butter into the flour until it resembles coarse sand.
  3. Add the milk and egg yolks, then mix until a soft dough forms. If it's too dry, add a splash more milk—no one judges.
  4. Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 1/8-inch thickness. Cut into 2-inch rounds and place them on the prepared baking sheets.
  5. Bake for 10–12 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden. Let cool completely before assembling.
  6. While the cookies cool, make the filling: In a small bowl, mix the almond butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla until smooth. If it’s too thick, add a drop of milk.
  7. Scoop a small amount of filling onto the center of each cookie, then top with another cookie to make a sandwich.
  8. Dip the edges of each cookie in water, then roll them in sprinkles. For an extra pop, add a few drops of food coloring to the water before dipping.
  9. Let the cookies set for at least 30 minutes before serving. They’re best when they’ve had time to firm up—like a good story, they need a little patience.

Dive into these cookies and experience a burst of color and crunch that’s as satisfying as it is nostalgic. Pair them with a glass of milk or a bold espresso for the ultimate snack-time combo.

Gluten-Free Rainbow Cookie Bites

Just when you thought life couldn’t get any brighter, these gluten-free rainbow cookie bites are here to add a splash of color—and flavor—to your day. These mini marvels are the ultimate snack for anyone who’s ever wondered, 'Why can’t cookies be as fun as a unicorn?'

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 20 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

Base Layers

  • a cup of gluten-free flour blend
  • a splash of almond milk
  • a couple of tablespoons of maple syrup
  • a pinch of salt
  • a teaspoon of vanilla extract

Rainbow Frosting

  • a half-cup of dairy-free cream cheese
  • a couple of tablespoons of powdered sugar
  • a few drops of food coloring in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple
  • a dash of lemon juice

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Grab a baking sheet and line it with parchment paper—no one wants a messy kitchen.
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine the gluten-free flour, a splash of almond milk, a couple of tablespoons of maple syrup, a pinch of salt, and a teaspoon of vanilla extract. Mix until a soft dough forms—think of it as the cookie version of a hug.
  3. Roll the dough into small balls, about the size of a marble, and place them on the baking sheet. Flatten each slightly with your fingers—this is where the magic happens.
  4. Bake for 12–15 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden. Let them cool completely before moving on to the next step—patience is key, like in a good relationship.
  5. While the cookies cool, prepare the frosting. In a separate bowl, mix the dairy-free cream cheese, a couple of tablespoons of powdered sugar, and a dash of lemon juice until smooth. Divide the mixture into six bowls and add different food coloring to each—red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple. This is where you get creative, so go wild!
  6. Once the cookies are cooled, use a piping bag or a spoon to spread a thin layer of colored frosting on each cookie. Don’t be shy—layer them up like you’re building a rainbow tower.
  7. Let the cookies set for at least an hour before serving—this is the secret to perfect texture. Pro tip: if they’re too soft, pop them in the fridge for 10 minutes.

Crunchy on the outside, chewy on the inside, and bursting with color, these bites are like confetti for your taste buds. Pair them with a glass of cold oat milk or serve them as a surprise at your next gathering—everyone will want the recipe.

Lemon Almond Rainbow Cookie

Waking up to the scent of lemon and almond is like getting a hug from your favorite bakery. These rainbow cookies are a burst of color, flavor, and fun that’ll make you question why you ever settled for plain old chocolate chip.

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 20 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

Dough

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of almond extract
  • a pinch of salt
  • a stick of unsalted butter, softened
  • a cup of granulated sugar
  • an egg

Lemon Glaze

  • the juice of two lemons
  • a cup of powdered sugar
  • a few drops of food coloring (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy—this takes about 2 minutes, but it’s worth the wait.
  3. Add the egg and almond extract, then mix until fully incorporated.
  4. Gradually add the flour and salt, mixing just until combined. Don’t overmix or you’ll end up with tough cookies.
  5. Divide the dough into six portions and roll each into a ball. Flatten them slightly on the baking sheet.
  6. Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden. Let them cool completely before glazing.
  7. While the cookies are cooling, whisk together the lemon juice and powdered sugar. Add a few drops of food coloring to each batch to create your rainbow hues.
  8. Once the cookies are cool, dip each one into the glaze and place them on a wire rack to set. For an extra zing, sprinkle a bit of lemon zest on top.
  9. Pro tip: If the glaze gets too thick, add a little water to thin it out. And if you’re feeling fancy, serve these with a side of fresh berries for a sweet, tangy combo.

Fruity, flaky, and full of personality, these cookies are a feast for the eyes and the taste buds. Try stacking them in a tower for a party centerpiece or hiding one in a lunchbox for a midday surprise.

Chocolate Rainbow Cookie Sandwich

Rumors say these cookies are so good, they might just make you question your life choices—like why you ever settled for plain old chocolate chip. But hey, we’re here to help you fix that.

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 30 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

For the Cookies

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a half cup of unsweetened cocoa powder
  • a stick of cold butter, cut into cubes
  • a quarter cup of granulated sugar
  • a quarter cup of brown sugar
  • one large egg
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a pinch of salt

For the Filling

  • a package of cream cheese, softened
  • a third cup of powdered sugar
  • a dash of vanilla extract
  • a few drops of food coloring (red, yellow, green, blue, purple)

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine flour, cocoa powder, and salt. Add butter and use your hands or a mixer to work it in until it resembles coarse sand.
  3. Mix in sugars, then add egg and vanilla. Beat until smooth and glossy.
  4. Roll out dough on a floured surface and cut into circles using a cookie cutter. Place on prepared sheets.
  5. Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until edges are set but centers are still soft. Let cool completely.
  6. While cookies cool, make the filling: beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla until smooth. Divide into small bowls and tint each with a different color.
  7. Once cookies are cool, spread a dollop of colored filling on the bottom of one cookie, then top with another. Press gently to form a sandwich.
  8. For a tip, use a piping bag for cleaner filling application. For extra flair, sprinkle crushed candy or sprinkles on top.

Holding one of these rainbow cookie sandwiches is like holding a tiny, edible piece of art. The rich, fudgy cookie gives way to a creamy, colorful center that’s as fun to look at as it is to eat.

Vanilla Bean Rainbow Cookie

Zesty, zingy, and zero regrets—these Vanilla Bean Rainbow Cookies are the kind of treat that makes you question why you ever settled for boring cookies in the first place.

Trending Right Now:  24 Delicious Easy Cupcake Recipes Amazing

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 20 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

The Essentials

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of milk
  • a couple of eggs
  • a stick of unsalted butter, softened
  • a heaping tablespoon of sugar
  • a pinch of salt
  • a teaspoon of vanilla extract
  • food coloring (pastel shades of pink, blue, green, and yellow)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. This is not a suggestion—it’s a command from your future cookie self.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. This usually takes about 2-3 minutes with a hand mixer, but if you’re feeling extra, do it by hand and call it a workout.
  3. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. If your batter looks like it’s about to throw a tantrum, add a splash of milk to smooth things out.
  4. Stir in the flour, salt, and vanilla extract. Don’t overmix—this isn’t a bread recipe, and we don’t want our cookies to be too dense.
  5. Divide the dough into four equal parts and tint each with a different pastel food coloring. Keep it subtle—no need to make your kitchen look like a neon dream.
  6. Roll each colored dough into a log, then slice into 1/4-inch thick rounds. Place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving a little space between each cookie.
  7. Bake for 12–15 minutes or until the edges are just starting to turn golden. Keep an eye on them—they can go from perfect to burnt faster than you can say 'vanilla bean.'

Scoop these cookies straight from the pan while they’re still slightly soft in the center—like a warm hug with a hint of floral sweetness. They’re perfect for dunking in coffee, stacking into a rainbow tower, or just pretending you’re a baker who knows what they’re doing.

Pistachio Rainbow Cookie Tart

Baked to perfection and bursting with color, this pistachio rainbow cookie tart is the kind of dessert that makes you want to throw a party just to eat it. It’s equal parts sweet, crunchy, and whimsical — like a rainbow took a bite out of a cookie and decided to stay for dinner.

Serving: 8 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients

For the crust

  • a cup of crushed rainbow cookies
  • a splash of melted butter
  • a pinch of salt

For the pistachio layer

  • a cup of finely chopped pistachios
  • a half cup of powdered sugar
  • a couple of tablespoons of cream
  • a dash of vanilla extract

For the rainbow layers

  • a cup of softened cream cheese
  • a third cup of powdered sugar
  • a few drops of food coloring (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)
  • a splash of milk

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a 9-inch tart pan with parchment paper and set aside.
  2. In a bowl, mix the crushed rainbow cookies with melted butter and a pinch of salt until it resembles wet sand. Press the mixture into the bottom of the tart pan and bake for 10 minutes to set.
  3. While the crust bakes, prepare the pistachio layer. In a food processor, blend the chopped pistachios with powdered sugar until smooth. Add a splash of cream and vanilla extract, then pulse until well combined. Spread this over the cooled crust.
  4. In a separate bowl, beat the cream cheese with powdered sugar and a splash of milk until fluffy. Divide the mixture into six small bowls and add different food coloring to each. Stir gently to create vibrant, pastel hues.
  5. Spoon each colored layer into the tart, alternating colors in a spiral or striped pattern. Use a knife to swirl them slightly for a more artistic look. Let the tart chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.
  6. Pro tip: If the layers are too stiff, add a little more milk. Also, don’t skip the salt in the crust — it brings out the flavors like a seasoned pro.
  7. Another tip: To get those perfect swirls, use a piping bag or even a spoon to carefully layer each color.
  8. Lastly, if you’re feeling extra fancy, top it with a few whole pistachios and a drizzle of honey for a touch of sweetness.

Scoop into a slice and savor the crunch of the crust, the creamy pistachio, and the bold pop of each rainbow layer. It’s like a candy store exploded in your mouth — but way better.

Caramel Drizzle Rainbow Cookie

Waffle cones are great, but have you ever tried a cookie that’s basically a rainbow in a bite? This caramel drizzle rainbow cookie is the kind of dessert that makes you question why you’ve never made it before.

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 10 minutes

Ingredients

For the cookies

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a half cup of unsalted butter, softened
  • a quarter cup of sugar
  • a pinch of salt
  • a splash of vanilla extract

For the filling

  • a third cup of raspberry jam
  • a few drops of food coloring (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)

For the caramel drizzle

  • a half cup of heavy cream
  • a stick of butter
  • a half cup of brown sugar
  • a dash of salt

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a mixing bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the vanilla and mix well.
  3. Gradually stir in the flour and salt. Knead the dough until smooth. Divide into 12 equal balls and flatten each into a disk.
  4. Place a small spoonful of raspberry jam in the center of each disk. Fold the edges over and pinch to seal. Roll into a ball and place on the baking sheet.
  5. Bake for 10 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool completely before handling.
  6. While the cookies cool, make the caramel: In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and stir until dissolved. Whisk in the cream and a pinch of salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes until thickened.
  7. Dip each cooled cookie into the caramel, letting any excess drip off. Place on a wire rack to set.
  8. Before drizzling, add a few drops of food coloring to the jam and spread between layers for a rainbow effect. Don’t skip this—it’s where the magic happens!
  9. If the caramel gets too thick, just add a splash of cream to loosen it up. And if you’re feeling fancy, top with a sprinkle of sea salt or crushed nuts.

Ahhh, these cookies are like a party in your mouth—crunchy on the outside, gooey on the inside, and dripping with caramel. Try serving them with a glass of milk or as a surprise for your favorite kid (or adult).

Raspberry Rainbow Cookie Trifle

Never underestimate the power of a rainbow cookie trifle to brighten your day—or your dessert table. This fruity, layered treat is a sweet rebellion against boring baked goods, and it’s here to make your week.

Serving: 8 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 0 minutes

Ingredients

Base

  • a pack of rainbow cookies (about 24 pieces)
  • a splash of milk (1/4 cup)

Filling

  • a tub of cream cheese (8 oz)
  • a couple of tablespoons of powdered sugar
  • a dash of vanilla extract
  • a big handful of fresh raspberries (about 1 cup)
  • a spoonful of raspberry jam

Topping

  • a container of whipped cream (16 oz)
  • a few extra raspberries for garnish

Instructions

  1. Start by crushing the rainbow cookies into small pieces using a food processor or your hands—this is where the fun begins.
  2. In a large bowl, mix the crushed cookies with a splash of milk until they form a moist, crumbly base. Press this into the bottom of a clear trifle dish or glass bowl.
  3. Take the cream cheese and beat it with a hand mixer until smooth. Add in the powdered sugar and vanilla extract, then mix until light and fluffy. This step is crucial—it’s the creamy heart of the trifle.
  4. Fold in the fresh raspberries and a spoonful of raspberry jam. The jam adds that extra tangy kick, so don’t skip it.
  5. Spoon a layer of the raspberry cream cheese mixture over the cookie base. For a more dramatic effect, use a spatula to spread it evenly.
  6. Repeat the layers: another layer of crushed cookies, then another layer of the raspberry filling. Aim for three layers total for maximum flavor.
  7. Top it all off with a generous dollop of whipped cream and a few fresh raspberries. You can even add a sprinkle of edible glitter for that extra sparkle.
  8. Let the trifle chill in the fridge for at least an hour before serving. This allows the flavors to meld and the textures to settle.

Scoop it up and watch your taste buds do a happy dance. The crunch of the cookies, the creamy raspberry swirls, and that final burst of tartness from the fresh berries make this trifle a standout. Serve it at a party, on a picnic, or just because you deserve something pretty and delicious.

Almond Joy Rainbow Cookie

Luscious, layered, and totally addictive, these Almond Joy Rainbow Cookies are the kind of treat that makes you question why you ever settled for plain old cookies. With a hint of coconut, a sprinkle of almonds, and a rainbow of color, they’re the ultimate snack for anyone who loves a little bit of everything.

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 30 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

For the cookies

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a half cup of unsalted butter, softened
  • a third cup of sugar
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a pinch of salt
  • a couple of tablespoons of shredded coconut
  • a handful of sliced almonds

For the glaze

  • a cup of powdered sugar
  • a couple of tablespoons of milk
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a few drops of food coloring (rainbow colors)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the vanilla and mix well.
  3. Stir in the flour, salt, and shredded coconut. Mix until just combined—don’t overmix.
  4. Fold in the sliced almonds by hand to avoid crushing them.
  5. Scoop tablespoon-sized balls of dough and place them on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them apart.
  6. Bake for 12–15 minutes or until the edges are golden brown. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
  7. While the cookies cool, make the glaze: in a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla. Add food coloring one drop at a time until you get a vibrant rainbow hue.
  8. Once the cookies are cool, drizzle the glaze over each one using a piping bag or a spoon. For extra flair, add a sprinkle of colored sugar or mini rainbow sprinkles.
  9. Let the glaze set for at least 10 minutes before serving.

Mouthwatering and oh-so-pretty, these cookies are like a party in every bite. The crisp exterior gives way to a soft, chewy center, while the glaze adds a sugary pop that’s impossible to resist. Try stacking them in a glass jar for a festive dessert display or pair them with a cold glass of milk for a sweet afternoon treat.

Mini Rainbow Cookie Cups

Today, I’m here to talk about the kind of dessert that makes you feel like a kid again—only with way more color and zero guilt. These mini rainbow cookie cups are the ultimate party in your mouth, and they’re just the thing to brighten up any day, especially if it’s Tuesday.

Serving: 24 | Prep Time: 20 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

For the Cookie Cups

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a half cup of unsalted butter, softened
  • a third cup of sugar
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a pinch of salt

For the Filling

  • a cup of cream cheese, softened
  • a half cup of powdered sugar
  • a splash of milk
  • a few drops of food coloring (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a muffin tin with paper liners—this is where the magic happens.
  2. In a mixing bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the vanilla and mix well.
  3. Gradually add the flour and salt, mixing until a soft dough forms. Don’t overmix—it’s okay if it’s a little lumpy.
  4. Tip: If the dough is too sticky, add a bit more flour.
  5. Divide the dough into 24 small balls and press each into the bottom of a muffin cup. Flatten slightly to form a cup shape.
  6. Bake for 10–12 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden. Let cool completely before filling.
  7. Tip: If the bottoms are too soft, chill them in the fridge for 10 minutes before filling.
  8. In a separate bowl, beat the cream cheese with powdered sugar and milk until smooth. Divide the mixture into six portions.
  9. Tip: Use different food colorings for each portion to create vibrant layers.
  10. Spoon a layer of colored cream cheese into each cup, then top with another layer of a different color. Repeat until each cup has 3–4 colorful layers.
  11. Once filled, refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to set. Serve chilled or at room temperature.

Unwrap these little gems and watch your taste buds do a happy dance. They’re soft, chewy, and packed with flavor—perfect for snacking, gifting, or just because.

Hazelnut Rainbow Cookie Cake

Kisses of color, layers of joy, and a hazelnut twist that’ll make your taste buds do the cha-cha. This rainbow cookie cake is a party in every bite—no confetti required, just a sprinkle of magic.

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 30 minutes | Cooking Time: 45 minutes

Ingredients

For the Crust

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of milk
  • a couple of tablespoons of unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • a pinch of salt
  • a dash of vanilla extract

For the Filling

  • a cup of hazelnut spread
  • a half-cup of powdered sugar
  • a splash of heavy cream

For the Rainbow Layers

  • a cup of flour
  • a half-cup of sugar
  • a teaspoon of baking powder
  • a quarter-teaspoon of salt
  • a stick of butter, softened
  • an egg
  • a splash of milk
  • food coloring in rainbow hues (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple)

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a 9-inch round cake pan with parchment paper and spray it with non-stick spray.
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, and baking powder. Add the cold butter and mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in the milk and vanilla extract until a dough forms. Press into the pan and bake for 15 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool completely.
  3. While the crust bakes, prepare the filling: In a large bowl, mix the hazelnut spread, powdered sugar, and heavy cream until smooth. Set aside.
  4. In another bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Add the softened butter, egg, and milk, and mix until a smooth batter forms. Divide the batter into six portions and tint each with a different food coloring—red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.
  5. Pour each colored batter into separate greased and lined mini loaf pans. Bake at 350°F for 12–15 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean. Let cool completely.
  6. Once cooled, slice each layer into two equal halves. Start assembling the cake by placing a layer of crust on a serving plate, then spread a thin layer of hazelnut filling. Stack a colored layer on top, add more filling, and repeat until all layers are used.
  7. Top with the final crust layer and finish with a generous swirl of hazelnut filling on top. Serve immediately.

Luscious, chewy, and bursting with color, this cake is a flavor fiesta. Pair it with a glass of cold milk or a scoop of vanilla ice cream for a treat that’s as fun to eat as it is to look at.

Mint Chocolate Rainbow Cookie

Zesty, zingy, and full of rainbow-colored joy, these mint chocolate rainbow cookies are the kind of treat that makes you want to dance in your kitchen. Think of them as the party animal of baked goods—bold, colorful, and always ready to impress.

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 12 minutes

Ingredients

For the Cookie Base

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of milk
  • a couple of eggs
  • a stick of unsalted butter, softened
  • a heaping tablespoon of cocoa powder
  • a pinch of salt

For the Mint Layer

  • a third of a cup of powdered sugar
  • a teaspoon of peppermint extract
  • a splash of heavy cream
  • a half cup of semisweet chocolate chips

For the Rainbow Frosting

  • a cup of butter, softened
  • a cup of confectioners’ sugar
  • a few drops of food coloring (in pastel shades)
  • a splash of milk

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
  3. Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt. Mix on low speed until just combined.
  4. Divide the dough into three equal parts. One part gets mixed with a bit of green food coloring for the mint layer, another gets a little pink, and the last stays neutral for the base.
  5. Roll out each portion of dough to about 1/4-inch thickness, then cut into circles using a cookie cutter. Place them on the prepared baking sheet.
  6. Bake for 10–12 minutes, or until the edges are set but the centers are still soft. Let cool completely before assembling.
  7. While the cookies cool, make the mint layer: In a small bowl, mix the powdered sugar, peppermint extract, and a splash of heavy cream until smooth. Spread a thin layer over the bottom cookie.
  8. Top with a layer of melted chocolate chips, then add a dollop of rainbow frosting. Press a second cookie on top to create a sandwich.
  9. Repeat with the remaining cookies, making sure to use different colors for each layer. For a fun twist, swirl the frosting for a marbled look.
  10. Let the cookies set in the fridge for at least 30 minutes before serving. This helps the layers hold together better.

Soft, chewy, and packed with flavor, these cookies are like a rainbow exploded in your mouth. Try them with a glass of cold milk or serve them as a whimsical dessert at a birthday party. Just don’t be surprised if they disappear faster than a magician’s rabbit.

Strawberry Rainbow Cookie Roll

Kisses of sweetness, a sprinkle of joy, and a dash of color—this Strawberry Rainbow Cookie Roll is the kind of dessert that makes you want to dance while eating it. It’s not just a treat; it’s a party on your plate, and you’re the guest of honor.

Serving: 8 | Prep Time: 30 minutes | Cooking Time: 15 minutes

Ingredients

For the Cookie

  • a cup of all-purpose flour
  • a splash of milk
  • a couple of eggs
  • a pinch of salt
  • a half-cup of sugar
  • a stick of melted butter
  • a teaspoon of vanilla extract

For the Filling

  • a jar of strawberry jam (or homemade if you're fancy)
  • a cup of cream cheese (softened)
  • a tablespoon of powdered sugar
  • a splash of lemon juice

For the Rainbow Swirl

  • a few drops of food coloring in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple
  • a small bowl of whipped cream

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and set it aside.
  2. In a large bowl, mix together the flour, salt, and sugar. Add the eggs, milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract. Whisk until smooth and silky—no lumps, no regrets.
  3. Pour the batter onto the prepared baking sheet and spread it evenly. Bake for 12–15 minutes or until the edges are golden and the center springs back when lightly touched.
  4. While the cookie is cooling, prepare the filling: In a separate bowl, beat the cream cheese until smooth. Add the powdered sugar and a splash of lemon juice, then mix until creamy and dreamy.
  5. Once the cookie is cooled, spread the strawberry jam over the surface, then layer the cream cheese mixture on top. Use a spatula to make sure it's even.
  6. To create the rainbow swirl, drizzle drops of food coloring into the whipped cream. Using a spoon, gently swirl the colored cream into the filling, creating a vibrant, marbled effect.
  7. Carefully roll the cookie from one end to the other, like a burrito. Slice into 8 pieces and serve immediately.

Elegant, playful, and perfectly chewy, these rolls are like a unicorn’s breakfast. Serve them with a side of glitter (or at least a smile) and watch the magic happen.

Coconut Macaroon Rainbow Cookie

Oozing with flavor and dripping with color, these Coconut Macaroon Rainbow Cookies are the kind of dessert that makes you question why you ever settled for plain old cookies in the first place.

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 20 minutes | Cooking Time: 25 minutes

Ingredients

For the macaroons

  • a cup of sweetened shredded coconut
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a couple of egg whites
  • a pinch of salt
  • a heaping tablespoon of powdered sugar

For the glaze

  • a half-cup of milk
  • a quarter-cup of corn syrup
  • a few drops of food coloring (multiple colors)
  • a teaspoon of butter
  • a splash of vanilla extract

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whip the egg whites until stiff peaks form.
  3. Gently fold in the sweetened shredded coconut, a splash of vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt.
  4. Spoon the mixture into small mounds on the prepared baking sheet—about 1 tablespoon each.
  5. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and crisp on the outside.
  6. While the macaroons cool, prepare the glaze by whisking together milk, corn syrup, and a splash of vanilla extract.
  7. Once the macaroons are out of the oven, drizzle a few drops of food coloring into the glaze and stir until vibrant.
  8. Dip the top of each macaroon into the glaze, then set them on a wire rack to let the glaze harden.
  9. If the glaze gets too thick, add a little more milk to thin it out—no one wants a sad, sticky cookie.
  10. Once set, stack the macaroons in a rainbow order and serve.

Kissed by the sun and kissed by the rainbow, these cookies are a crunchy, chewy, and oh-so-satisfying treat. Try stacking them in a tower for a show-stopping dessert or hiding one in a bag for a surprise snack.

Blueberry Rainbow Cookie Tartlet

Unwrap the sweetness of a summer day with this vibrant Blueberry Rainbow Cookie Tartlet—because who says dessert can't be a little bit magical (and a lot of fun)?

Serving: 12 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 30 minutes

Ingredients

For the Base

  • a cup of rainbow cookie crumbs
  • a stick of melted butter
  • a splash of vanilla extract

For the Filling

  • a cup of fresh blueberries
  • a half cup of sugar
  • a tablespoon of lemon juice
  • a pinch of salt
  • a few tablespoons of cornstarch

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a mini tart pan with 12 parchment cups.
  2. In a bowl, mix the rainbow cookie crumbs with melted butter and a splash of vanilla extract until it resembles wet sand.
  3. Press the mixture into each tart cup, making sure it’s evenly packed for a sturdy base.
  4. In a saucepan, combine blueberries, sugar, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly.
  5. When the blueberries start to break down, add a few tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with a little water. Keep stirring until the filling thickens—this usually takes about 5-7 minutes.
  6. Pour the blueberry filling into the prepared tart shells, filling them about three-quarters full.
  7. Bake for 25–30 minutes, or until the filling is set and the edges are lightly golden.
  8. Let the tarts cool completely before serving. They’re best enjoyed chilled!

Garnish with a sprig of mint or a sprinkle of edible glitter for extra flair. These tartlets are a dreamy blend of sweet, tangy, and crunchy—perfect for a snack that feels like a celebration.

Rainbow Cookie Mousse Cup

Dive into a dessert that’s as colorful as it is delicious—this Rainbow Cookie Mousse Cup is a celebration in every bite, with layers that’ll make your taste buds do the happy dance.

Serving: 6 | Prep Time: 25 minutes | Cooking Time: 0 minutes

Ingredients

For the Base

  • a few rainbow cookies crumbled into a fine mix
  • a splash of vanilla extract
  • a couple of tablespoons of melted butter

For the Mousse Layers

  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 3/4 cup powdered sugar
  • a pinch of salt
  • 1 tablespoon cocoa powder
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1 package instant chocolate pudding mix
  • 1 cup whipped cream
  • 1/2 cup crushed rainbow cookies

Instructions

  1. In a mixing bowl, combine the crumbled rainbow cookies, vanilla extract, and melted butter to form a sticky base. Press the mixture into the bottom of 6 small cups or ramekins.
  2. In a separate bowl, beat the heavy cream, powdered sugar, and a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form. Set aside.
  3. In a large bowl, whisk together the milk, cocoa powder, and pudding mix until thickened, about 2 minutes. Fold in the whipped cream gently to create a smooth chocolate mousse layer.
  4. Spoon the chocolate mousse over the cookie base and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or until firm.
  5. Once set, top each cup with a layer of whipped cream and a sprinkle of crushed rainbow cookies for a colorful finish.

Scoop up this dreamy treat and savor the soft, silky mousse contrasting with the crunchy cookie base—it’s like a party in your mouth. Serve it with a side of joy, or maybe a spoon, because you’ll want to dig in right away.
